architecture.mechanism: Exploit the high arsenic‑binding capacity of locally abundant iron‑oxide minerals (laterite) and carbonaceous biochar, which adsorb arsenic through surface complexation and co‑precipitation, enabling passive removal without external chemicals.
architecture.intervention: Construct a gravity‑fed, multi‑layer filter cartridge from sand, laterite/iron‑oxide soil, and biochar, assembled in a simple ceramic or PVC housing that requires no electricity or chemical dosing.
architecture.expected_effect: Achieve ≥90 % reduction in dissolved arsenic, bringing concentrations below the WHO limit of 10 µg/L, with measurable improvement in water quality.
architecture.falsification_test: Conduct a field trial measuring arsenic levels in influent and effluent water using inexpensive test strips; if post‑filter arsenic remains above 10 µg/L or flow rate drops >50 % within 24 h, the design fails.
